title: Compiler Flags
concept: Complete reference of XIOM compiler flags — optimization levels, output control, debugging, and advanced compilation options.
why: The compiler has dozens of flags controlling every aspect of compilation. Knowing them gives you precise control over the build process and output.
theory:
## XIOM Compiler Flag Reference

### Optimization Flags

```sh
-O0            # No optimization (default for debug)
-O1            # Basic optimization
-O2            # Standard optimization
-O3            # Aggressive optimization
-Os            # Optimize for size
-Oz            # Optimize aggressively for size
```

### Output Flags

```sh
-o <file>      # Output file name
--emit-ir      # Emit LLVM IR instead of binary
--emit-asm     # Emit assembly instead of binary
--emit-ast     # Emit AST dump (debugging)
--emit-tokens  # Emit token stream (debugging)
```

### Debugging Flags

```sh
-g             # Include debug symbols
--backtrace    # Show backtrace on panic/trap
--verbose      # Show detailed compilation steps
--time         # Show time spent in each compilation phase
```

### Contract Control

```sh
--no-contracts       # Strip all contract checks
--runtime-contracts  # Keep contract checks in optimized builds
```

### Warnings and Lints

```sh
-W all          # Enable all warnings
-W error        # Treat warnings as errors
-W no-unused    # Disable unused variable warnings
--deny <lint>   # Deny specific lint
--allow <lint>  # Allow specific lint
```

### Target Flags

```sh
--target <triple>     # Cross-compile target
--target-cpu <cpu>    # Target specific CPU
--target-features <f> # Enable target features
```

### Advanced Flags

```sh
--incremental   # Enable incremental compilation
--parallel N    # Number of parallel jobs (default: CPU cores)
--lto           # Enable Link-Time Optimization
--no-default-libs  # Don't link default libraries
--static        # Produce statically linked binary
--dynamic       # Produce dynamically linked binary
```

### Flag Categories

```sh
xiom help flags            # List all compiler flags
xiom help flags optimization # Show optimization flags only
xiom help flags debugging    # Show debugging flags only
```
syntax_ref:
xiom build -O2 --target x86_64-linux-gnu -o myapp main.xi
xiom build --emit-ir --verbose main.xi
xiom build -W error --no-contracts --release main.xi
tips: Use `--emit-ir` to understand what code LLVM sees — great for optimization debugging
`--time` tells you which compilation phase is slowest — focus optimization there
Chain flags with intent: `xiom build -O3 --release --static --no-contracts` for a production binary
Use `xiom help flags` as your cheat sheet — there's no need to memorize all flags
common_mistakes: Using too many optimization flags together — some conflict (e.g., -O3 + -Os)
Enabling all warnings (-W all) without checking what they catch — can produce noise
Forgetting --runtime-contracts when you need safety in optimized builds
